test_text: Ich gehe nicht raus, null es regnet. (because)
meaning: I am not going out because it is raining.
grammar_tip: denn (because) takes position 0. Verb stays in position 2: ...denn es regnet.

test_text: Er kommt nicht, null er ist krank. (because)
meaning: He is not coming because he is sick.
grammar_tip: denn connects two main clauses: ...denn er ist krank.

test_text: Wir bleiben zu Hause, null das Wetter ist schlecht. (because)
meaning: We are staying at home because the weather is bad.

test_text: Sie kauft ein Eis, null es ist sehr heiß. (because)
meaning: She buys an ice cream because it is very hot.

test_text: Ich nehme den Regenschirm mit, null es regnet. (because)
meaning: I'll take the umbrella along because it's raining.

test_text: null regnet heute den ganzen Tag. (It)
meaning: It is raining all day today.
grammar_tip: Weather verbs use 'Es': Es regnet, Es schneit.

meaning: Tomorrow it will snow.
How is the weather today?
The sun is shining beautifully.
Today it is very windy.
grammar_tip: Weather adjectives use 'es ist': Es ist windig.

meaning: In winter it is cold.
grammar_tip: Weather adjectives use 'es ist': Es ist kalt.

meaning: Munich is located in the south.
grammar_tip: Compass directions: im Norden, im Süden, im Osten, im Westen.

meaning: Hamburg is located in the north.
Berlin is located in the east.
Cologne is located in the west.
I travel to the south.
We are flying to the south.

test_text: Der Wind kommt null dem Norden. (out of)
meaning: The wind comes from the north.
It is raining today.
Tomorrow it snows.
The sun is shining.
Yesterday it rained.
grammar_tip: Perfekt of regnen: es hat geregnet.

test_text: Es hat in der Nacht null. (gesneit -> geschneit)
meaning: It snowed in the night.
The sun shone.
grammar_tip: Partizip II of scheinen is irregular: geschienen.

test_text: Das Wetter null gestern sehr schön. (was)
meaning: The weather was very nice yesterday.
grammar_tip: Präteritum of sein: das Wetter (es) -> war.

meaning: It was very cold yesterday.
I'll take the suitcase along.
Are you taking an umbrella along?

test_text: Warum bleibst du zu Hause? - null ich krank bin. (Weil or Denn? Let's use 'Weil' if position 0 doesn't fit, but prompt asks for 'Denn' usually in main clauses. Let's make it two sentences) Ich bleibe zu Hause, null ich bin krank.
meaning: Why are you staying at home? - I am staying at home, because I am sick.
grammar_tip: denn: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.

meaning: Why are you not going for a walk?

test_text: Es ist kalt, null bleibe ich zu Hause. (therefore)
meaning: It is cold, therefore I am staying at home.
grammar_tip: deshalb takes position 1: deshalb bleibe ich...

test_text: Wir fahren null die Ostsee. (to/at the)
tip: Preposition for bodies of water (Akkusativ for direction)
meaning: We travel to the Baltic Sea.

test_text: Wir machen Urlaub null der Nordsee. (at the)
tip: Preposition for bodies of water (Dativ for location)
meaning: We are vacationing at the North Sea.

test_text: Wir wandern null den Bergen. (in the)
meaning: We hike in the mountains.

test_text: Wir fahren null die Berge. (into the)
meaning: We travel to the mountains.

test_text: Das Wetter in Norddeutschland null meistens schlecht. (is)
meaning: The weather in Northern Germany is mostly bad.

test_text: Wie null das Wetter morgen? (will be / becomes)
meaning: How will the weather be tomorrow?
grammar_tip: werden is often used for future/change: es wird.

meaning: Tomorrow it will rain.

test_text: null Grad haben wir heute? (How many)
meaning: How many degrees do we have today?

meaning: I love summer, because it is hot.

meaning: The wind comes from the west.
